sentences.text: Petitioner is the sole accused in Crime No.212/2023 of Aranmula Police Station, Pathanamthitta.
He filed this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. praying for quashing all further proceedings against him.

The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Section 376(2)(e) and 354B of IPC.
2.

The prosecution case is that the accused after promising to give employment to the defacto complainant, called her to his hospital on 29.1.2023 at about 8.30 p.m., and when she requested for water he had given her water in a bottle containing some intoxicating substance.

After drinking the water, when she became unconscious, she was allegedly raped by the petitioner at about 1.00 a.m.,
on 30.1.2023.

3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner now the entire dispute between the petitioner and the defacto complainant is settled and therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.

4. The defacto complainant/2nd respondent also filed an affidavit stating that the entire dispute between the petitioner and the defacto complainant is settled and that she does not want to proceed with the case against the petitioner.
5. Though notice was served on the 2 nd respondent, she did not turn up.
The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the petition.
However, upon 2026:KER:9599 instructions, he submitted that the defato complainant had given signed statement to the SHO in tune with the averments in the affidavit filed before this Court.

6. In the FI statement, it is alleged that as requested by the defacto complainant, the petitioner gave her water containing some intoxicating substance and when she became unconscious, she was abused by somebody.

On the next morning, when she woke up, she called the petitioner over telephone and told him that she was abused by somebody and also that she is going to create a scene, the petitioner allegedly told her that he himself abused her, that she could continue there as a permanent employee and requested not to make any scene.
In the FI statement, she further states that in spite of such assurance made by the petitioner she left the service of the petitioner and returned to her residence.
7. Though the alleged incident was on 30.1.2023, the matter was reported to the police only on 4.3.2023, more than two months after the alleged incident.
No satisfactory explanation is offered for the above delay of more than two months in reporting the matter to the police.
The above conduct of the defacto complainant in not reporting the matter to the police in time casts serious doubt on her claim that the petitioner abused her without her knowledge or consent.
In other words, there is every reason to believe that the relationship between the petitioner and the defacto complainant was a consensual one.

The above 2026:KER:9599 conclusion is fortified by the fact that now the defacto Dr. Sajeev vs State Of Kerala on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75923006/
2 complainant filed an affidavit stating that she does not want to proceed against the petitioner.
In the above circumstances, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings against the petitioner and as such the Crl.M.C. is liable to be allowed.
In the result, this Crl.MC. is allowed.

All further proceedings against he petitioner in Crime No.212/2023 of Aranmula Police Station, Pathanamthitta, stands quashed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
